title: MongoDB Transactions
summary: Configure MongoTransactionManager and understand rollback and proxy boundaries.

sources.title: Engineering Digest: @Transactional Annotation in Spring Boot Example in Hindi | @Enabletransactionmanagement
Spring Data MongoDB: sessions and transactions

richText: A transaction groups database operations so they commit together or roll back together. Atomic means the group succeeds completely or leaves no committed partial result.
The journal creation flow saves an entry and then adds its reference to User. A transaction prevents a failed user save from leaving only the entry committed.
MongoDB already makes a single-document write atomic. Use a multi-document transaction when one business rule requires several document writes to succeed together.
Multi-document transactions require a replica set or a supported sharded cluster. A standalone local MongoDB server does not provide this transaction setup.
A replica set is a group of MongoDB servers maintaining copies of the same data. Configure the driver to discover the correct deployment.
MongoTransactionManager uses the MongoDatabaseFactory to manage MongoDB sessions and transactions. @Transactional alone does not supply a MongoDB transaction manager.
The manager and participating repositories must use the same database factory. When several transaction managers exist, select the intended manager explicitly.
The course explicitly enables transaction management. This configuration makes that requirement visible in the learning example.
Put the boundary on a service
Call the public service method through the Spring bean. Default transaction handling uses a proxy, an object that intercepts the call and starts the transaction.
A call from one method to another method on the same instance bypasses that proxy. Adding @Transactional to the called method does not create a new boundary for that self-call.
By default, RuntimeException and Error trigger rollback. A checked exception does not. Specify rollbackFor when a checked exception should also roll back.
Let failures reach the transaction boundary. Catching an exception and returning normally can allow a transaction to commit.
A successful database commit does not roll back an email or external HTTP call. Keep such side effects outside assumptions about database atomicity.
